message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most famous American composers across different eras and genres:

| Era / Genre | Composer | Notable Works |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| **Classical (19th–early 20th c.)** | **John Philip Sousa** | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “Washington Post March” |
| | **George Gershwin** | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| | **Scott Joplin** | “Maple Leaf Rag,” “The Entertainer” |
| | **Aaron Copland** | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| **Contemporary Classical** | **Philip Glass** | “Glassworks,” “Einstein on the Beach” |
| | **Steve Reich** | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| | **John Adams** | “Short Ride in a Fast Machine,” “Nixon in China” |
| | **Jennifer Higdon** | “Blue Cathedral,” “Piano Concerto” |
| **Jazz & Popular** | **Duke Ellington** | “Mood Indigo,” “It Don’t Mean a Thing (If It Ain’t Got That Swing)” |
| | **Miles Davis** | “Kind of Blue,” “Bitches Brew” |
| | **Herbie Hancock** | “Cantaloupe Island,” “Head Hunters” |
| | **Bob Dylan** | “Blowin’ in the Wind,” “Like a Rolling Stone” |

These composers have left indelible marks on American music, influencing not only their own genres but also the broader cultural landscape.
